summary.business: LTTS provides AI, digital, and engineering research & development (ER&D) services to global enterprises across three segments — Mobility (Automotive, Aerospace, Rail, Trucks & Off-Highway), Sustainability (Discrete Manufacturing & Industrial Products, Process Industries), and Tech (MedTech, Media & Tech, Software & Platforms). It partners with OEMs, Tier-1s and technology majors on product engineering, digital engineering, and platform-led AI solutions rather than selling its own branded end products.

currentContext.strengths: Ranked #1 pure-play engineering services company (rated by Zinnov, ISG, and Everest)|Large patent portfolio: 1,706 patents filed, including 237 in AI and GenAI, underpinning IP-led differentiation|Deep, sticky client relationships: 417 global clients including 69 Fortune 500 companies and 57 of the Global 100 R&D spenders|Global delivery scale: presence in 25 countries, 22 global design centers, 31 global sales offices, and 98 innovation labs|Sustained large-deal momentum — average TCV of ~USD 200 million across six consecutive quarters, including USD 100Mn+ and USD 75Mn+ wins|Strategic technology partnerships (SiMa.ai, NVIDIA, MIT Media Lab) reinforcing its AI/Agentic AI and Engineering Intelligence (EI) capability build-out|Repeated third-party leadership recognitions across ER&D, digital engineering, semiconductor, and MedTech service categories (HFS, ISG, Avasant, CII)
currentContext.strategies: "Pivot on Growth" operating philosophy anchored in five strategic vectors: For Clients (deepening partnerships across the lifecycle), Of Technology (AI/digital/platform-driven innovation), Of Teams (future-ready talent), For Investors (consistent, profitable, sustainable returns), and Of Self (a sharper, more agile organization)|Lakshya 31 five-year plan built around six large technology bets: Software Defined Mobility (SDM); Plant Buildout & Modernization; Energy & Industrial Automation/Digital Manufacturing; Next-Gen Compute & AI Infra; Software Platforms & EI; and MedTech|Engineering Intelligence (EI) framework at the core of strategy, built on three pillars — Physical AI (mechatronics + autonomous intelligence at the edge), Manufacturing AI (intelligence embedded in industrial systems), and Engineering AI (software-defined, intelligent product development) — integrating engineering, AI and digital technologies|Divested the Smart World and Communication (SWC) business as part of portfolio sharpening, to reallocate capital toward high-growth, high-margin areas and accelerate investment in Engineering Intelligence|Conscious shift toward higher-value, future-ready offerings — exiting select non-strategic engagements and sharpening focus on high-margin, scalable opportunities|Talent strategy centered on the Global Engineering Academy for AI/digital upskilling and reskilling, and an internal leadership pipeline (Leaders League program, ALTUM succession framework)|Continued scaling of proprietary AI and digital engineering platforms — FusionWorld.ai, PLxAI, AiNexus, and TrackEi — supporting the AI-first, platform-led delivery model|AGM Notice proposes a final dividend of Rs 40 per equity share (face value Rs 2) for FY26, subject to shareholder approval; no separate capital-allocation philosophy narrative appears in this routed section beyond the dividend declaration.
currentContext.expansion: LTTS' expansion is delivery-footprint-led rather than physical-plant-led: as of March 31, 2026 the Company operated across 25 countries via 22 global design centers, 31 global sales offices and 98 innovation labs equipped with cutting-edge technologies for R&D. During the year, LTTS partnered with a leading global energy major to set up and scale a new Digital and Power Expertise Center in India, positioning itself as the engineering services and technology partner building this next-generation global capability hub across power, data and digital domains. The company's Lakshya 31 plan also names 'Plant Build Out & Modernisation' among its six large technology-investment bets, extending its ER&D delivery capability into industrial plant-side engineering for clients.
currentContext.mdna: India strengthening its position as a global ER&D hub, with LTTS positioned to capitalise on expanding offshoring opportunities and rising domestic innovation-led investment|Diversified geographic presence benefiting from large-scale investment in energy, smart infrastructure and industrial transformation, particularly in the United States, Europe and Japan|Growth outlook described as balanced and resilient, supported by increasing engineering intensity across industries|Operating environment remains complex — persistent macroeconomic uncertainty, geopolitical developments, evolving regulatory frameworks and supply-chain realignments continue to influence enterprise spending and decision cycles|Mobility: shaped by shifts in Software Defined Mobility (SDM) adoption and OEM spending cycles — muted demand in H1 followed by growing traction in SDV, electrification platforms and next-generation mobility solutions|Sustainability: robust, double-digit growth driven by global investment in energy transition, data centers, plant engineering and industrial automation; remains the segment with the highest margin|Tech: resilient amid uncertain investment priorities and demand cycles, supported by rising adoption of AI-led engineering, platform engineering and digital transformation across semiconductors, telecom and MedTech|Large-deal momentum sustained at an average TCV of ~USD 200 million for six consecutive quarters through Q4FY26|40% rise in large-deal value in FY26, finalizing USD 855 million in transformative engagements across all three segments|Robust pipeline of next-generation programs across global OEMs and Tier-1s cited for the Mobility segment|Marquee ~USD 100 million engagement cited as reaffirming LTTS' position in the Sustainability segment

risks.note: A broadening digital threat landscape, including possible AI-driven attacks, software-supply-chain vulnerabilities and identity-based threats, could lead to unauthorized access to proprietary data, causing financial loss, reputational harm and regulatory non-compliance.
Risk of non-compliance with evolving data privacy laws and contractual obligations across the jurisdictions LTTS operates and delivers services in.

Wars, tariffs and trade restrictions, inflation and cyclical downturns can cause clients to delay projects or embark on cost-reduction initiatives, impacting LTTS' business operations, revenue growth and margins.
High dependence on a specific segment, customer or geography creates concentration risk; LTTS monitors revenue contribution by geography and by top clients to manage this exposure.

Challenges in attracting and retaining skilled talent, high attrition in certain areas, rising demand for onsite client support, and stringent/costlier visa regulations can impact business growth, delivery capability and client satisfaction.

risks.risk: Evolving and disruptive technologies (incl. client in-sourcing/GCC trend)
risks.note: Difficulty keeping pace with customer expectations for innovation (e.g. AI) could impact growth momentum; the broader IT/ER&D industry also faces the growing trend of multinational clients opening their own captive Global Capability Centers (GCCs), a structural demand risk for outsourced engineering services.
Operating globally exposes LTTS to foreign exchange risk, managed through a Board-approved Forex Risk Management policy, natural hedging and active hedging instruments.

one-line thesis: A clean "steady execution" start to FY27 on a rebased portfolio: constant-currency revenue +1.5% QoQ / +1.9% YoY with EBIT margin up to 15.7% (+50 bps QoQ, +200 bps YoY) and net income +17.4% YoY, as Sustainability (+4.3% QoQ, ~29% margin) and a recovering Mobility (+2.3% QoQ) offset a soft, SWC-exited Tech (11.5% margin). The narrative is fully pivoted to "Engineering Intelligence" — an Anthropic/Claude tie-up, a Munich EI center, and 100 forward-deployment engineers — and management explicitly reconfirmed sequential revenue AND margin growth every quarter, mid-16% EBIT by/before Q4FY27, and the Lakshya-31 13-15% 5-year revenue CAGR at 16-17% margins.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy):
| Metric | Q1FY27 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue ($) | $309.9 mn | +1.9% CC | +1.5% QoQ CC (vs $305.9 mn Q4); realized Rs 94.86/$ |
| Revenue (Rs) | Rs 2,940 cr | +11.5% | +2.9% QoQ |
| EBIT / margin | Rs ~462 cr / 15.7% | +200 bps | +50 bps QoQ |
| PAT (net income) | Rs 352 cr / 12% of rev | +17.4% | +1.5% QoQ |
| EPS (continuing) | Rs 33.17 (ann. Rs 132.68) | +~15% vs FY26 Rs 115.89 | |
| Order book (TCV) | ~$100 mn large-deal TCV | — | A few large deals slipped to early Q2 |
| Cash / net debt | Rs 3,394 cr cash & investments | Net cash | vs Rs 3,555 cr Q4; FCF Rs 540 cr (153% of NI) |
> One-offs: Other income only Rs 14.7 cr (down QoQ) on forex/hedge losses — expect this range for next few quarters. ETR 26% (guiding 26.2-26.7%). Dollar revenue is on a rebased portfolio (SWC/Smart World exit + prior "empty calories" pruning), so YoY dollar growth understates underlying.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Revenue growth:** 13-15% CAGR over the next 5 years (Lakshya 31); **sequential revenue growth every quarter** reconfirmed; growth committed for Q2 (no annual outlook given by policy).
- **Margin:** 16-17% EBIT band (5-yr aspiration); **mid-16% EBIT on or before Q4 FY27**; sequential margin expansion each quarter of FY27.
- **Segment:** Sustainability double-digit YoY growth for FY27 (reconfirmed); Tech to return to growth from Q2; Mobility gradual improvement through the year.
- **Cash / tax / WC:** FCF ~90-95% of net income for FY27 (Q1 was 153%, a working-capital outperformance); ETR 26.2-26.7%; combined DSO 80-85 days.
- **Corporate action:** SWC (Smart World) divestment to conclude in Q2 FY27.
order book & pipeline: Large-deal TCV ~$100 mn in Q1, with a few large wins pushed to early Q2 (not broad-based; partly Europe summer + client-specific timing). Pipeline described as strengthened vs last quarter/year. Named wins/expansions: Emerson (global System Integrator & tech-development partner), a leading Aerospace connectivity platform, an EV manufacturer expansion (exterior/lighting), an Ophthalmology/microsurgery offshore engineering center, and a leading global energy company (ramping). A "significant" Telecom deal expected to close early Q2 with immediate ramp; more medical-domain deals in negotiation. Flexible ramp-up model lets execution start on deal close.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Mobility:** +2.3% QoQ, broad-based (Aero & Rail + T&OH led; US Auto recovered — "worst from US auto behind us"). Margin 15.6% (slight dip on onsite ramp of new programs). Europe OEM/Tier-1 still weak (China exposure vanishing, model-year pushouts) but LTTS positioned to win vendor consolidation from a lower cost base. No sub-split disclosed anymore.
- **Sustainability:** +4.3% QoQ, +11.3% YoY; margin 29.1% (+40 bps), most profitable. Plant Engineering strong across Upstream O&G/LNG/Chemicals; Industrial Products strong across Data Centers, Electrical Equipment, Motion & Robotics, Automation. Ainfonix platform gaining adoption. Could have grown more with more talent (hiring).
- **Tech:** soft quarter, margin 11.5%; now 30.6% of revenue (was 34.4% a yr ago) — reflects SWC exit + Sustainability outgrowth. MedTech program concluded + next delayed; a medical deal and Telecom deal in pipeline. Returns to growth from Q2; not expected back to ~34% mix.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Engineering Intelligence (EI):** the core thesis — "6-layer AI cake" (energy, chips, infra, data engineering, AI models, applications) mapped to the Six Technology Bets. Toolkit: PlxAI, AiNexus, AiTest, Ainfonix (aid), AgenticIQ (autonomy/agents), Track AI / Physical AI (embedded). Consulting entry via MIT Media Labs AI Readiness Index → paid AI-maturity assessments → rollout.
- **Anthropic/Claude partnership:** integrating Claude models across engineering processes and LTTS platforms (AgenticIQ, PlxAI); plus Databricks tie-up. Positions LTTS as "owner's engineer" (e.g., compressing a client's 36-40-month design cycle to 15-18 months).
- **New capabilities:** Munich EI Center (Europe's first), 244 AI patents (1,757 total), 100 forward-deployment engineers, FinTech first Private-Equity client, PharmaWiseAI for life-sciences R&D.
6a. moat & competitive position (optiona:
- **Time-to-market lead:** management asserts LTTS is "6 to 9 months ahead of competition" in EI — a differentiation window, not a permanent moat, requiring continuous reinvestment.
- **Pricing power / non-commodity positioning:** "Nobody has ever come back and say reduce your rates… we are not a commodity player" — differentiated higher-end engineering supports margin expansion even as some AI productivity is passed on to win deals.
- **Diversification as defense:** three Mobility sectors × three geographies (US/Europe/ROW) cushioned the Europe-auto downturn — evidenced by US Auto + T&OH/Aero offsetting Europe this quarter.
margins & cost dynamics: EBIT 15.7% (+50 bps QoQ, +200 bps YoY). Three margin levers reiterated: (1) mix shift to higher-margin Sustainability/Mobility + improving Tech, (2) EI-led delivery productivity, (3) operational excellence + disciplined SG&A. Rupee depreciation (Rs 94.86/$, -1.5% QoQ) a tailwind but partly offset by hedge losses in other income. Offshore mix 53.9% (room to improve); T&M mix down to 64.9% as fixed-price/outcome deals rise. Headcount steady 23,845; attrition 14.7%.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): Asset-light — no physical-capex guidance; "expansion" is EI centers (Munich), platforms, patents and talent (forward-deployment engineers, Sustainability hiring). Watch: large-deal slippage from Q1→Q2 and Telecom-deal close/ramp timing.
capital allocation: Net cash Rs 3,394 cr; strong FCF (Rs 540 cr, 153% of NI this quarter; 90-95% guided for year). Continued investment in EI and the Six Technology Bets. Portfolio pruning ongoing (SWC divestment concluding Q2). EPS +~15% YoY on continuing operations reflects mix + prudent capital allocation. No buyback/dividend change flagged on call.
risks & watch-items:
- Europe Auto/Tier-1 weakness (China demand evaporating, model-year pushouts) — recovery is "to be played out."
- Large-deal timing slippage (a few Q1 wins moved to Q2); Telecom deal must close/ramp as promised.
- Tech segment must actually inflect to growth from Q2.
- AI cannibalization debate: LTTS argues AI expands (not replaces) engineering work, but must keep passing some productivity to clients to win — margin/volume balance to monitor.
- Forex/hedge-loss drag on other income for next few quarters.
- Middle East geopolitics (small direct exposure; some Q1 execution delay).
management quality / tone: Confident, candid, detail-rich; deliberately gives a 5-year outlook + quarterly growth commitment but declines annual guidance (by investor feedback). Amit Chadha personally did 48 client meetings in Apr-May. Transparent on deal slippage and the SWC exit. "Paranoid" framing on staying ahead of AI disruption. Reconfirms prior commitments rather than resetting them — credibility-positive.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The lower dollar revenue base vs a year ago is engineered (SWC exit + "empty calories" pruning), so headline dollar growth understates the healthier, higher-margin underlying book.
- Management's counter to "AI kills IT/ER&D": the two large model providers and a hyperscaler have each set up their own services companies — if services were dying, they wouldn't.
- "Owner's engineer" repositioning (via Claude + tools) is a scope/pricing upgrade, not just a productivity story — LTTS increasingly owns the client's process/IP, not just staffing it.
- Sustainability could have grown more but for talent constraints — a hiring bottleneck, not a demand one.
- Company now commits to sequential margin AND revenue growth every quarter — an unusually specific bar to be held to.

themes.title: AI-led IT services & ER&D transformation
themes.need: Q1FY27 split the bucket three ways: a soft large-cap core, a re-accelerating mid-cap tier, and an outright business-model change. TCS grew constant currency only +0.4% QoQ / +3.2% YoY despite $9.5bn of TCV (including an ~$800mn net-new SKF mega-deal), and its AI-services book annualising $2.6bn (+13.6% QoQ) saw incremental adds DECELERATE from +$125mn to +$75mn - AI is still project revenue, not annuity. WIPRO is the laggard (+0.9% YoY cc, margin -120bps to 16.0%, Q2 guided -1.5% to +0.5%). Mid-caps are outgrowing: TECHM grew +6.6% YoY cc with every vertical up and an 11th consecutive quarter of margin expansion (14.4%, +330bps); MPHASIS's pipeline is at an all-time high, 2.8x its size at the Mphasis.ai launch and +28% YoY, with AI-led deals now 70% of it (from 12%) and BFS pipeline +100% YoY, and its new Tria platform closed multiple opportunities within seven weeks of launch; FRACTAL lifted net income +92% YoY on INR 912.5cr revenue at NRR 117% with zero churn (though only +9% cc, dragged by TMT -22%); KPITTECH won $349M of new deals with 21% of pipeline now productized AI/SDV solutions. Structurally, HCLTECH is entering the AI-datacenter business with an initial investment of up to INR 3,500cr and a 50MW long-term ambition, and PERSISTENT is buying Nagarro at EUR 1.27bn EV to build a $2.9bn / 46,000-person group - European scale is now bought, not built. The new cost line is visas: TATAELXSI crossed INR 1,000cr of quarterly revenue for the first time (INR 1,021.1cr) yet EBIT fell 330bps QoQ, with 220-230bps of it onsite/subcontractor investment the CFO said cannot be passed to customers.
themes.driver: MPHASIS's guide that 'Q2 is positioned to deliver the best sequential constant currency growth we have delivered in three years' is the most falsifiable claim in the sector; then HCLTECH's AI-datacenter build, the PERSISTENT-Nagarro close, and whether TCS's AI incremental adds re-accelerate off +$75mn.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: LTTS provides AI, digital, and engineering research & development (ER&D) services to global enterprises across three segments — Mobility (Automotive, Aerospace, Rail, Trucks & Off-Highway), Sustainability (Discrete Manufacturing & Industrial Products, Process Industries), and Tech (MedTech, Media & Tech, Software & Platforms). It partners with OEMs, Tier-1s and technology majors on product engineering, digital engineering, and platform-led AI solutions rather than selling its own branded end products.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body:
- **Mobility:** +2.3% QoQ, broad-based (Aero & Rail + T&OH led; US Auto recovered — "worst from US auto behind us"). Margin 15.6% (slight dip on onsite ramp of new programs). Europe OEM/Tier-1 still weak (China exposure vanishing, model-year pushouts) but LTTS positioned to win vendor consolidation from a lower cost base. No sub-split disclosed anymore.
- **Sustainability:** +4.3% QoQ, +11.3% YoY; margin 29.1% (+40 bps), most profitable. Plant Engineering strong across Upstream O&G/LNG/Chemicals; Industrial Products strong across Data Centers, Electrical Equipment, Motion & Robotics, Automation. Ainfonix platform gaining adoption. Could have grown more with more talent (hiring).
- **Tech:** soft quarter, margin 11.5%; now 30.6% of revenue (was 34.4% a yr ago) — reflects SWC exit + Sustainability outgrowth. MedTech program concluded + next delayed; a medical deal and Telecom deal in pipeline. Returns to growth from Q2; not expected back to ~34% mix.

- **AI Platforms (company-wide):** PLxAI, AiNexus

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Large-deal TCV ~$100 mn in Q1, with a few large wins pushed to early Q2 (not broad-based; partly Europe summer + client-specific timing). Pipeline described as strengthened vs last quarter/year. Named wins/expansions: Emerson (global System Integrator & tech-development partner), a leading Aerospace connectivity platform, an EV manufacturer expansion (exterior/lighting), an Ophthalmology/microsurgery offshore engineering center, and a leading global energy company (ramping). A "significant" Telecom deal expected to close early Q2 with immediate ramp; more medical-domain deals in negotiation. Flexible ramp-up model lets execution start on deal close.

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **Revenue growth:** 13-15% CAGR over the next 5 years (Lakshya 31); **sequential revenue growth every quarter** reconfirmed; growth committed for Q2 (no annual outlook given by policy).
- **Margin:** 16-17% EBIT band (5-yr aspiration); **mid-16% EBIT on or before Q4 FY27**; sequential margin expansion each quarter of FY27.
- **Segment:** Sustainability double-digit YoY growth for FY27 (reconfirmed); Tech to return to growth from Q2; Mobility gradual improvement through the year.
- **Cash / tax / WC:** FCF ~90-95% of net income for FY27 (Q1 was 153%, a working-capital outperformance); ETR 26.2-26.7%; combined DSO 80-85 days.
- **Corporate action:** SWC (Smart World) divestment to conclude in Q2 FY27.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **Engineering Intelligence (EI):** the core thesis — "6-layer AI cake" (energy, chips, infra, data engineering, AI models, applications) mapped to the Six Technology Bets. Toolkit: PlxAI, AiNexus, AiTest, Ainfonix (aid), AgenticIQ (autonomy/agents), Track AI / Physical AI (embedded). Consulting entry via MIT Media Labs AI Readiness Index → paid AI-maturity assessments → rollout.
- **Anthropic/Claude partnership:** integrating Claude models across engineering processes and LTTS platforms (AgenticIQ, PlxAI); plus Databricks tie-up. Positions LTTS as "owner's engineer" (e.g., compressing a client's 36-40-month design cycle to 15-18 months).
- **New capabilities:** Munich EI Center (Europe's first), 244 AI patents (1,757 total), 100 forward-deployment engineers, FinTech first Private-Equity client, PharmaWiseAI for life-sciences R&D.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India strengthening its position as a global ER&D hub, with LTTS positioned to capitalise on expanding offshoring opportunities and rising domestic innovation-led investment
- Diversified geographic presence benefiting from large-scale investment in energy, smart infrastructure and industrial transformation, particularly in the United States, Europe and Japan
- Growth outlook described as balanced and resilient, supported by increasing engineering intensity across industries
- Operating environment remains complex — persistent macroeconomic uncertainty, geopolitical developments, evolving regulatory frameworks and supply-chain realignments continue to influence enterprise spending and decision cycles
- Mobility: shaped by shifts in Software Defined Mobility (SDM) adoption and OEM spending cycles — muted demand in H1 followed by growing traction in SDV, electrification platforms and next-generation mobility solutions
- Sustainability: robust, double-digit growth driven by global investment in energy transition, data centers, plant engineering and industrial automation; remains the segment with the highest margin
- Tech: resilient amid uncertain investment priorities and demand cycles, supported by rising adoption of AI-led engineering, platform engineering and digital transformation across semiconductors, telecom and MedTech
- Large-deal momentum sustained at an average TCV of ~USD 200 million for six consecutive quarters through Q4FY26
- 40% rise in large-deal value in FY26, finalizing USD 855 million in transformative engagements across all three segments
- Robust pipeline of next-generation programs across global OEMs and Tier-1s cited for the Mobility segment
- Marquee ~USD 100 million engagement cited as reaffirming LTTS' position in the Sustainability segment

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [AI partnerships] "LTTS partnered with Anthropic to leverage Claude and deliver AI-powered Engineering Intelligence for products, services and industrial solutions", plus "a strategic go-to-market partnership with Databricks... to co-develop and deliver Industrial AI solutions that advance Engineering Intelligence (EI) for asset-intensive enterprises".
